subject: MAP: FindWell embeddings + reranker performance plan and close timeline
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@findwell.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff: FindWell embeddings + reranker perf plan

Aisha —

Thanks for taking the time last week. As discussed, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on the two performance streams you want validated: the embeddings ingestion endpoint (bulk and QPS characteristics) and the reranker endpoint (latency under concurrent ranking requests).

High-level goals we propose for the evaluation:
- Latency: P50/P95/P99 for embeddings (per vector) and reranker (per query) under expected concurrency
- Throughput: steady-state QPS and peak sustained throughput for both endpoints
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) for reranker streaming responses
- Concurrency scaling: behavior across 8 / 32 / 128 concurrent clients
- Failure modes: graceful degradation plan and fallback to smaller reranker model

Proposed deliverables & ownership:
- Redwood load test plan + script (we own) — run week of 6/22, deliver raw CSV + perf_summary.pdf
- FindWell will provide representative production query set (sampled) and expected concurrency targets by 6/18
- Joint review and tuning session 6/25
- Pilot sign-off (runbook + SLOs) by 7/10

Attached: MAP spreadsheet (map_findwell_v1.xlsx) includes timeline and acceptance criteria. If that timeline looks ok I'll schedule the 6/25 review and kick off the load run after we get the sample queries.

Thanks —
Rafael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@findwell.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: FindWell embeddings + reranker perf plan

Rafael —

Thanks, this looks like the right structure. A few clarifications from our side:
- Concurrency target: realistic production load is ~80 concurrent users, but peak flash-loads can hit ~200 for bursts. Please test 8 / 64 / 200 if possible.
- Embeddings pattern: mixed batch and single-vector calls. We'll provide a 100k sample split (80/20) for batch vs single.
- Reranker: we stream top-K scoring back to the app. TTFT is critical — sub-250ms preferred for initial token in the default 8-ranker model.

We will upload the sample query set to the Drive link by EOD 6/18. 6/25 review works for us.

--
Aisha Khan
Head of Search, FindWell

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: platform@findwell.ai
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: FindWell embeddings + reranker perf plan — load run results (initial)

Team / Aisha —

We completed the first full load run against the FindWell staging cluster today. Attachments: findwell_loadtest_jun25.csv (raw samples) and perf_summary_findwell.pdf (slide-summary + charts). High-level results below (all numbers measured in staging with Redwood Dedicated profile: 4x A100 equivalent):

Embedding endpoint (mixed workload; 80% single, 20% batch):
- Steady-state throughput: 1,150 req/s (single-vector equiv)
- P50 latency: 12 ms / vector; P95: 46 ms; P99: 110 ms
- Peak sustained (60s): 1,620 req/s before queueing increases
- Cost proxy: ~0.000012 tokens-equivalent per vector (see CSV)

Reranker endpoint (top-8 reranker, streamed):
- Concurrency sweep: 8 / 64 / 128 / 200 simulated clients
- At 8 clients: P95 latency = 48 ms; TTFT = 38 ms; throughput 520 qps
- At 64 clients: P95 latency = 170 ms; TTFT = 120 ms; throughput 480 qps (slight qps drop due to batching interaction)
- At 128 clients: P95 latency = 220 ms; TTFT = 200 ms; throughput 410 qps
- At 200 clients: P95 latency = 480 ms; TTFT = 390 ms; throughput 290 qps (degrading but within graceful fallback range)

Notes and interpretation:
- The reranker meets the <250ms TTFT and P95 target up to ~128 clients. At 200 clients we breach the preferred TTFT but latency growth is consistent and predictable — A/B fallback to a smaller reranker reduces P95 by ~40% in a separate run (see perf_summary).
- Embeddings show excellent single-vector p95 numbers and scale linearly; batching gives good throughput gains for bulk jobs.
- We captured request traces (rerank_trace_ids.txt) for the 200-client run to deep-dive slow paths (KV cache thrash and kernel queueing).

Next steps:
- Tune batch sizing and KV cache settings, rerun a focused 200-client tuning test by 6/29.
- Prepare MAP update with acceptance gates (pilot SLOs, fallback config) — Marissa to own.

-Grace
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@findwell.ai>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Updated MAP + close timeline (FindWell)

Aisha / team —

I've updated the MAP spreadsheet with the measured acceptance criteria and an executable close timeline. Summary below — full MAP in the Drive link.

Acceptance gates (pass/fail):
- Embeddings: P95 <= 60 ms single-vector; bulk throughput >= 1,200 req/s sustained
- Reranker: TTFT <= 250 ms and P95 <= 250 ms at 128 concurrent clients; fallback to compact-reranker reduces P95 <= 150 ms if exceeded
- Stability: error rate < 0.1% over a 10-minute window during peak runs

Committed timeline and owners:
- 6/29: tuning run for 200-client case (Grace)
- 7/2: deliver tuned perf_summary + updated traces (Grace)
- 7/6: pilot sign-up and canonical run with FindWell production sample (Rafael + Karthik)
- 7/10: pilot acceptance review (Aisha, Redwood eng, product) — go/no-go decision
- 7/16: finalize commercial terms (pricing worksheet)
- 7/22: contract signature target

If FindWell can accept the acceptance gates above, we should be able to keep the 7/22 close target. Rafael: please confirm if we should push any dates to accommodate procurement on their side.

Regards —
Marissa Cole
VP, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
